**141. What Power Automate for desktop version is required for the bring-your-own-machine option?**

Power Automate for desktop version 2.61.132.2xxx or later (a recent, specific minimum version is required). [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Configure computer use as an agent tool] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/4-configure-computer-use

**142. What does the access control allow list restrict, and does it also restrict navigation?**

It restricts which URLs/apps the agent can interact with (supports wildcards like *.contoso.com); it restricts interaction, not navigation — the model can still open unlisted sites, it just can't interact with them. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Configure computer use as an agent tool] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/4-configure-computer-use

**143. What does the side panel show when advanced Dataverse logging is enabled (the default), per the unit?**

Session replay, Activity, Summary, Websites/applications visited, Credentials used, and an option to export session logs. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Monitor and supervise computer use execution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/5-monitor-computer-use

**144. Under what activity term do computer use operations appear in Microsoft Purview, and does this depend on logging verbosity/retention settings?**

They appear under the activity term 'CUAOperation,' and this logging is independent of the verbosity/retention settings configured for computer use. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Monitor and supervise computer use execution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/5-monitor-computer-use

**145. What is 'Session replay' in the monitoring side panel used for?**

To visually replay the recorded screen actions taken during a computer use session, for review/audit purposes. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Monitor and supervise computer use execution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/5-monitor-computer-use

**146. Per the module assessment, what happens to desktop flows on a machine once computer use is enabled there?**

Desktop flow functionality is disabled on that machine. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Module assessment] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/6-knowledge-check

**147. What five topics does the module summary say were covered regarding computer use?**

Understanding computer use fundamentals, evaluating scenario fit, configuring it as a tool (machines, credentials, access control), and monitoring/supervising its execution. [SRC: Automate desktop and web tasks with computer use in Copilot Studio — Summary] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/automate-desktop-web-tasks-computer-use-copilot-studio/7-summary

**148. What two tool types share the pattern of connecting an agent directly to a known API via a schema-defined interface, without custom integration code?**

Connector tools and REST API tools. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/introduction/

**149. What's the difference in reuse scope between a custom connector and a REST API tool?**

A custom connector is built in the Power Apps maker portal and is reusable across Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps, and Azure Logic Apps. A REST API tool is created in Copilot Studio and stored at the environment level — usable by other agents in that environment, but not by other Power Platform products. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand connector and REST API tools in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/understand-connector-rest-api-tools/

**150. What determines which tool the generative orchestrator invokes at runtime?**

It evaluates the user's message against each tool's name and description and selects the most appropriate action to fulfill the task. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand connector and REST API tools in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/understand-connector-rest-api-tools/

**151. What's the most common reason an agent fails to invoke the right connector or REST API tool?**

A weak or vague tool description. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand connector and REST API tools in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/understand-connector-rest-api-tools/

**152. When should you invoke a connector from within a topic node instead of at the agent level?**

When you need deterministic, controlled execution regardless of user phrasing, bypassing generative orchestration. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand connector and REST API tools in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/understand-connector-rest-api-tools/

**153. What permission must be granted before another maker can add an existing custom connector as an agent tool?**

Can view (or Can edit) permission, shared with them via the Power Apps maker portal. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add prebuilt and custom connector tools to an agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/add-connector-tools/

**154. What happens if a maker tries to add a premium connector without a premium Copilot Studio license?**

Copilot Studio displays a licensing prompt. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add prebuilt and custom connector tools to an agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/add-connector-tools/

**155. What deployment requirement applies specifically to maker-provided credentials for a connector tool?**

The agent must be deployed on an authenticated channel, or the maker-provided credentials option won't appear in the configuration. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for connector tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/configure-connector-authentication/

**156. Give an example of when user-provided credentials are the right choice for a connector tool.**

When each user has their own account in the connected system and should act as themselves — e.g., sending email through Office 365 Outlook from the individual employee's mailbox. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for connector tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/configure-connector-authentication/

**157. What SSO limitation applies to connector tools in Microsoft Teams?**

SSO isn't supported for connector tools when the agent uses custom Active Directory (AD) authentication in Teams — users must sign in to each connector manually. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for connector tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/configure-connector-authentication/

**158. What specification format do REST API tools require, and what happens if you upload OpenAPI v3?**

OpenAPI v2 (Swagger) in JSON format; Copilot Studio automatically converts an OpenAPI v3 spec to v2 during upload. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add a REST API tool using an OpenAPI specification] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/add-rest-api-tool/

**159. Why should you select only the endpoints an agent needs when creating a REST API tool from a large OpenAPI spec?**

A smaller, focused tool surface area improves orchestration accuracy and limits unintended access to the API. [SRC: Take action in external systems using connector and REST API agent tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add a REST API tool using an OpenAPI specification] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-external-systems-connector-rest-api-tools-copilot-studio/add-rest-api-tool/

**160. How do Copilot connectors make external content available to agents?**

By ingesting and semantically indexing it into Microsoft Graph, so it becomes searchable and citable across Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Microsoft Search. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Choose between Copilot connector and Power Platform connector knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/choose-knowledge-source-approach/

**161. How does a real-time Power Platform connector knowledge source retrieve data?**

Each query triggers a live API call through the connector at the moment the agent needs an answer; no data is copied into Microsoft 365. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Choose between Copilot connector and Power Platform connector knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/choose-knowledge-source-approach/

**162. Which knowledge source type supports inline citations, and which doesn't?**

Copilot connectors support inline citations because content is indexed. Real-time Power Platform connectors don't offer inherent citation support. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Choose between Copilot connector and Power Platform connector knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/choose-knowledge-source-approach/

**163. Who must configure a Copilot connector before a maker can add it to an agent?**

A tenant administrator, in the Microsoft 365 admin center — not the individual maker. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot connectors as knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/add-copilot-connector-knowledge/

**164. What Microsoft Graph scope must be added to a channel's manual authentication configuration so a published agent can retrieve Copilot connector content?**

ExternalItem.Read.All [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot connectors as knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/add-copilot-connector-knowledge/

**165. What does the 'Tenant graph grounding with semantic search' setting do?**

For tenants with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, it improves knowledge retrieval quality from Copilot connectors by using semantic search to surface more contextually relevant results. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot connectors as knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/add-copilot-connector-knowledge/

**166. What does Copilot Studio index for a real-time connector knowledge source, versus the actual data?**

Only metadata (table and column names) is indexed; actual data retrieval happens live at runtime under the asking user's own authenticated identity, honoring source-system access controls. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure Power Platform connectors as real-time knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/configure-realtime-knowledge-sources/

**167. What controls which connectors are available for real-time knowledge sources, and what happens if one is blocked?**

Data loss prevention (DLP) policies; a blocked connector won't appear as an option, and any existing knowledge source using it stops working. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure Power Platform connectors as real-time knowledge sources] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/configure-realtime-knowledge-sources/

**168. What is the critical rule for adding Azure AI Search as a knowledge source, and what's the risk of ignoring it?**

Always use the Create new connection dialog; manually entering the endpoint URL and API key can create a faulty environment-level connection that blocks every agent in the environment from adding Azure AI Search knowledge sources. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to Azure AI Search] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/connect-azure-ai-search/

**169. Which Azure AI Search authentication type does Microsoft recommend, and why?**

Microsoft Entra ID Integrated — it uses the signed-in user's identity, removing key-management overhead. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to Azure AI Search] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/connect-azure-ai-search/

**170. How many Azure AI Search vector indexes can be added per data connection?**

Only one index per connection. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to Azure AI Search] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/connect-azure-ai-search/

**171. What Azure AI Search feature improves ranking for natural-language queries that don't map to exact keywords?**

The semantic ranker — it must already be enabled in Azure AI Search and supported by the service tier before it can be activated in Copilot Studio. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to Azure AI Search] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/connect-azure-ai-search/

**172. How does Copilot Studio determine the citation URL field for an Azure AI Search knowledge source?**

It checks for a field named metadata_storage_path first; if that field isn't present, it uses whichever field contains a complete URL. [SRC: Ground agents in enterprise knowledge using connectors and Azure AI Search in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to Azure AI Search] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/ground-agents-enterprise-knowledge-connectors-azure-ai-search-copilot-studio/connect-azure-ai-search/

**173. What does an MCP server host, according to the module?**

One or more tools (functions the agent can call), and optionally resources (data the agent can read) and prompts (reusable prompt templates). [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand MCP integration in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/understand-mcp-integration/

**174. In MCP terminology, what role does Copilot Studio play?**

The MCP client — it connects to the server, discovers what it offers, and lets the agent's orchestrator select and invoke tools during a conversation. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand MCP integration in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/understand-mcp-integration/

**175. What is the key advantage of MCP's standardization compared to building a connector or Power Automate bridge for each backend system?**

A single MCP server can expose many tools, and the discovery/invocation handshake is identical regardless of which backend system sits behind it. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand MCP integration in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/understand-mcp-integration/

**176. What must a maker provide when creating a new MCP server connection in Copilot Studio?**

The MCP server's endpoint URL, given to the maker by the team hosting the server. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to an MCP server] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/connect-mcp-server/

**177. What happens during the MCP 'discovery handshake'?**

Copilot Studio queries the server for its tool manifest — the list of tools it exposes, along with each tool's name, description, and input/output schema. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to an MCP server] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/connect-mcp-server/

**178. Can a maker edit an MCP tool's description within Copilot Studio?**

Generally no — the description is owned and returned by the MCP server; unclear descriptions should be reported to the team maintaining the server rather than edited in Copilot Studio. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to an MCP server] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/connect-mcp-server/

**179. What's the recommended troubleshooting order when an MCP tool isn't invoked as expected?**

Check the tool is enabled, then check the description for ambiguity, then verify authentication to the server is correctly configured. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect an agent to an MCP server] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/connect-mcp-server/

**180. Which MCP authentication type is recommended for production scenarios requiring per-user access control?**

OAuth 2.0 / Microsoft Entra ID, passing through the signed-in user's identity. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for MCP server connections] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/configure-mcp-authentication/

**181. What is a typical symptom of a missed authentication scope when publishing an agent with an authenticated MCP connection to a channel?**

The MCP tool appears configured correctly during authoring but silently fails to return results (or returns an authentication error) once published, because the necessary scope wasn't granted at publish time. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for MCP server connections] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/configure-mcp-authentication/

**182. What happens to an agent's enabled MCP tools if the server rotates its API key and the Copilot Studio connection isn't updated to match?**

Every enabled tool from that server typically stops functioning until the credential is corrected. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure authentication for MCP server connections] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/configure-mcp-authentication/

**183. Should every tool an MCP server exposes be enabled for every connecting agent?**

No — apply least-privilege: per agent, enable only the subset of tools relevant to that agent's intended use, leaving administrative or engineering-only tools disabled. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Enable and manage MCP tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/enable-manage-mcp-tools/

**184. What should a maker review before enabling an MCP tool that has side effects, such as creating a record?**

Its description and input/output schema from discovery — asking what it does when invoked, whether it needs confirmation, and what data it needs and returns. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Enable and manage MCP tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/enable-manage-mcp-tools/

**185. If an MCP server adds a new tool to its exposed set, does a connected agent gain access to it automatically?**

No — the maker must review it on the Tools page and explicitly enable it if appropriate. [SRC: Integrate agents with external systems via MCP in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Enable and manage MCP tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/integrate-agents-external-systems-mcp-copilot-studio/enable-manage-mcp-tools/

**186. What two forms do multi-agent solutions take in Copilot Studio?**

Child agents (built inside the main agent, sharing its context and lifecycle) and connected agents (separately deployed agents the main agent communicates with at runtime). [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand multi-agent architectures in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/2-understand-multi-agent-architectures/

**187. What rule-of-thumb action-count threshold signals that an agent's routing accuracy may start degrading?**

Around 30–40 choices of action (topics, tools, and connected agents combined) — not a hard limit, but a practical signal to validate against your own evaluations. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand multi-agent architectures in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/2-understand-multi-agent-architectures/

**188. Besides routing accuracy, name structural reasons the module gives for considering a multi-agent architecture.**

Multiple teams manage different parts independently; components need separate authentication/security/model configuration; different ALM processes are needed per part; a capability is reused across multiple orchestrators; or components must be published and maintained separately. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand multi-agent architectures in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/2-understand-multi-agent-architectures/

**189. When is a single-agent architecture the appropriate choice, per the module?**

When the solution responds to a single intent or task, a small cohesive team manages it, no separate configuration/authentication/deployment is needed, and the agent won't be reused in other orchestrators. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand multi-agent architectures in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/2-understand-multi-agent-architectures/

**190. What is a child agent, and how is its lifecycle tied to the parent?**

A focused workflow built directly inside the parent agent that shares the parent's context; it has no independent publishing lifecycle and is deployed whenever the parent is. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using child agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/3-design-agent-organization/

**191. What is a connected agent, and how does the main agent treat it?**

A separately published agent with its own orchestration, tools, knowledge, and deployment lifecycle; from the main agent's perspective it looks like 'a tool with a description.' [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**192. What extra cost does every connected agent introduce that child agents don't?**

Orchestration hops — extra round-trips where the main agent identifies and calls the connected agent, which the connected agent's own orchestration layer then processes, adding latency. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**193. What defines the orchestrator/subagent coordination pattern?**

A primary orchestrator agent receives the user's input and dynamically decides at runtime which specialist (sub)agent is best suited to handle it, rather than following a fixed sequence. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**194. What defines the workflow-oriented coordination pattern, and what are its two forms?**

A predefined sequence or parallel set of steps controlled by a workflow engine; its two forms are serial workflow (steps complete strictly in order) and concurrent workflow (multiple agents run in parallel and their outputs combine). [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**195. List the five connection options for adding an external agent to a Copilot Studio orchestrator.**

Existing Copilot Studio agent; Microsoft Foundry agent (preview); Microsoft Fabric Data agent (preview); Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agent (preview); and A2A protocol agent. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**196. Which connection option connects to a partner or cross-platform agent that manages its own reasoning outside Microsoft infrastructure?**

An A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol agent. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**197. What governance responsibility remains with the orchestrator's maker when connecting to another team's agent?**

Accountability for appropriate data flows, having permissions/approvals in place before sensitive actions occur, and configuring observability to correlate transcripts for debugging and audits — even though the capability belongs to another team's agent. [SRC: Design multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design multi-agent solutions using connected agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-multi-agent-solutions-copilot-studio/4-select-multi-agent-orchestration-pattern/

**198. What makes a child agent different from a topic inside Copilot Studio?**

A topic handles a single conversational intent with a defined node sequence, while a child agent has its own instructions, tools, and knowledge sources and uses its own orchestration when the parent delegates to it. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Understand child agents in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/2-understand-child-agents/

**199. How does a parent agent decide whether to delegate to a child agent by default?**

It evaluates the incoming request against the child agent's description. If the description matches, the parent delegates and the child responds using its own instructions, tools, and knowledge. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Understand child agents in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/2-understand-child-agents/

**200. What naming guidance does the unit give for child agents?**

Use a descriptive, bounded name such as "Order Status Agent" so the agent is easy to identify in logs and during debugging; avoid generic names like "Support Helper" or "Agent 1." [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Create and configure a child agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/3-create-configure-child-agent/

**201. Which routing choice should you use when delegation must be predictable regardless of user phrasing?**

Use explicit trigger events. The unit presents them as deterministic routing for cases such as redirects from topics, inactivity, plan completion, and other specific events. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Create and configure a child agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/3-create-configure-child-agent/

**202. What is the difference between a child agent description and its instructions?**

The description controls routing—when the agent is called. Instructions control execution—how it behaves once it is called. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Configure child agent inputs, outputs, and trigger behavior] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/4-configure-child-agent-inputs-outputs-triggers/

**203. When should you keep a tool or knowledge source scoped only to a child agent?**

As a default practice, scope resources to the most specific agent that needs them. Add them to the parent only if they genuinely must be available across all domains. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Configure child agent inputs, outputs, and trigger behavior] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/4-configure-child-agent-inputs-outputs-triggers/

**204. Which After running option fits a child agent whose outputs must feed the next orchestration step?**

Choose Don't respond, the default. The parent continues its orchestration plan without sending a user message, which fits cases like another child-agent call, a condition check, or another action. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Configure child agent inputs, outputs, and trigger behavior] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/4-configure-child-agent-inputs-outputs-triggers/

**205. What does Show activity map when testing help you see?**

It shows the orchestrator's execution plan in real time, including which child agent was selected, what inputs were passed, and what it returned. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Test and manage child agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/5-test-manage-child-agents/

**206. What happens after a topic redirects to a child agent and the child finishes?**

The topic resumes at the node immediately after the redirect, and the child agent's output values are automatically placed in topic variables for later nodes to use. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Test and manage child agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/5-test-manage-child-agents/

**207. Why is disabling a child agent usually safer than deleting it when future reuse is possible?**

Disabling takes the agent out of rotation without removing it. Deletion permanently removes the child agent and its instructions, inputs, outputs, trigger settings, and scoped tools or knowledge, and it can't be undone. [SRC: Delegate agent tasks using child agents in Copilot Studio — Test and manage child agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/delegate-agent-tasks-child-agents-copilot-studio/5-test-manage-child-agents/

**208. What is a connected agent in Copilot Studio?**

A separately published, independently managed agent that an orchestrator connects to and delegates tasks to. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Understand connected agents in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/2-understand-connected-agents/

**209. By default, what context does the orchestrator pass to a connected agent?**

Conversation history is passed by default so the connected agent can respond in context, and this can be disabled per connection. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Understand connected agents in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/2-understand-connected-agents/

**210. Why are overlapping connected-agent descriptions risky?**

Because routing relies on descriptions, overlapping descriptions can confuse the orchestrator and lead to misrouting. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Understand connected agents in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/2-understand-connected-agents/

**211. What prerequisites must be met before connecting an existing Copilot Studio agent?**

The target agent and orchestrator must be in the same Power Platform environment, the target must have a published version, connections must be enabled, and you must be the owner or have shared access. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect an existing Copilot Studio agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/3-connect-copilot-studio-agent/

**212. Which setting on the target Copilot Studio agent allows other agents to connect to it?**

Turn on Let other agents connect to and use this one in the target agent's General settings. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect an existing Copilot Studio agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/3-connect-copilot-studio-agent/

**213. If you edit a connected Copilot Studio agent's description inside the orchestrator, does that change the source agent?**

No. The orchestrator stores its own local description copy, and local edits don't affect the connected agent itself or other orchestrators. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect an existing Copilot Studio agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/3-connect-copilot-studio-agent/

**214. What two key values do you need to connect a Microsoft Foundry agent?**

The Microsoft Foundry project endpoint URL and the agent's unique agent ID. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect a Microsoft Foundry agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/4-connect-foundry-agent/

**215. What portal requirement applies to Foundry agents used in Copilot Studio connections?**

They must be created and published in the new Microsoft Foundry portal; agents from the legacy Azure AI Studio portal return a 404 when Copilot Studio tries to connect. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect a Microsoft Foundry agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/4-connect-foundry-agent/

**216. Which query languages do Fabric Data agents use for different data sources?**

SQL for lakehouses and warehouses, DAX for Power BI semantic models, and KQL for KQL databases. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect a Microsoft Fabric Data agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/5-connect-fabric-data-agent/

**217. What routing constraint is called out for connected Fabric Data agents?**

They are supported only through generative orchestration based on descriptions; topic-level agent redirect nodes to Fabric Data agents aren't currently supported. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Connect a Microsoft Fabric Data agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/5-connect-fabric-data-agent/

**218. What testing aid shows which connected agent handled a prompt and how the orchestrator routed it?**

Enable Show activity map when testing; the activity map shows which connected agent generated the response and what routing decision the orchestrator made. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Manage and test your connected agent solution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/6-manage-test-connected-agent-solution/

**219. What happens when you disable a connected agent?**

It becomes inactive for all users and triggers, the orchestrator won't route to it, and all connection configuration is preserved. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Manage and test your connected agent solution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/6-manage-test-connected-agent-solution/

**220. Why might you need both the orchestrator transcript and the connected agent transcript during debugging?**

Because connected agents generate separate transcripts, reviewing both may be necessary to reconstruct an end-to-end interaction. [SRC: Build multi-agent solutions using connected agents in Copilot Studio — Manage and test your connected agent solution] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-multi-agent-solutions-connected-agents-copilot-studio/6-manage-test-connected-agent-solution/

**221. What is the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol?**

An open standard for agent-to-agent communication across platform boundaries, purpose-built for delegating a task to another agent that manages its own reasoning, tools, and responses independently. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/2-understand-a2a-protocol/

**222. What information does an A2A agent card provide, and where is it typically published?**

It is a JSON discovery document, typically at `/.well-known/agent.json`, that describes the agent's name, purpose, capabilities, and communication endpoint. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/2-understand-a2a-protocol/

**223. What do context IDs do in A2A?**

They maintain conversation continuity across agent boundaries by associating delegated tasks with the same ongoing conversation across multiple turns. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/2-understand-a2a-protocol/

**224. When should you choose A2A instead of a connector or MCP?**

Choose A2A when the external capability is a standalone agent with its own model, tools, and orchestration—especially across platforms, across organizations, or when multi-turn context matters. Use a connector for raw API data and MCP for orchestrator-controlled tool invocations. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Understand the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/2-understand-a2a-protocol/

**225. What single piece of information do you need from the external agent owner to begin an A2A connection in Copilot Studio?**

The endpoint URL. Copilot Studio derives the agent-card discovery URL (`/.well-known/agent.json`) automatically from that endpoint. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect a Copilot Studio agent to an A2A-enabled agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/3-connect-a2a-enabled-agent/

**226. What authentication options are supported for A2A connections in Copilot Studio?**

None, API key, and OAuth 2.0. The source says None is appropriate only for sample, sandbox, or development scenarios—not for production integrations. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect a Copilot Studio agent to an A2A-enabled agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/3-connect-a2a-enabled-agent/

**227. What makes an effective A2A agent description in the orchestrator?**

It should be specific, distinct, and action-oriented, because the orchestrator uses the description to decide when to delegate requests to that agent. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Connect a Copilot Studio agent to an A2A-enabled agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/3-connect-a2a-enabled-agent/

**228. How do you verify in Copilot Studio that a test prompt was delegated to an A2A agent?**

Open Test your agent, send a prompt that should route to the A2A agent, and review the activity log to confirm the delegation and inspect the returned response. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test and validate an A2A agent connection] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/4-test-validate-a2a-connection/

**229. What information is included in an A2A message payload according to the source?**

Each message includes a context ID, message IDs, locale, conversation history from the current session by default, and structured message content parts such as text, metadata, and tool call results where applicable. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test and validate an A2A agent connection] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/4-test-validate-a2a-connection/

**230. What responsible-use checks does the source say to review before enabling an A2A integration for live users?**

Review what is in the conversation history, confirm the data processing terms with the external organization, assess the external agent's reliability and accuracy, ensure logging and monitoring exist, and confirm there is a human-oversight path for high-stakes scenarios. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test and validate an A2A agent connection] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/4-test-validate-a2a-connection/

**231. What are some common A2A troubleshooting patterns from the source?**

No delegation usually points to routing/description issues; authentication errors point to incorrect credentials or header/OAuth configuration; agent-card discovery issues point to a bad endpoint or missing card; connection errors can indicate network or gateway problems. [SRC: Build cross-platform multi-agent solutions using the Agent2Agent protocol in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test and validate an A2A agent connection] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/build-cross-platform-multi-agent-solutions-agent2agent-copilot-studio/4-test-validate-a2a-connection/

**281. What is a Copilot agent according to the unit?**

A Copilot agent is a modular, instruction-driven AI component designed to perform a specific business task or workflow; it follows structured instructions, leverages organizational data, and uses tools and connectors to take action. Sequential workflow, parallel evaluation, feedback-loop iteration, and orchestrated interaction. Instruction-level extensibility, skill and capability extensibility, integration extensibility, and pro-code agent extensibility in Visual Studio Code. **284. In the unit, what do skills define for an agent?**

Skills define what an agent can do, such as retrieval skills from enterprise content sources, action-oriented skills through connectors or custom APIs, multi-step workflows, and added domain knowledge to improve accuracy. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design extensible agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-extensibility-copilot-studio/

**285. Why does the unit recommend a modular agent architecture?**

Because interchangeable components such as instructions, skills, integrations, and tools enable faster updates and versioning, reuse across multiple agents, and better isolation for compliance and secure design. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design extensible agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-extensibility-copilot-studio/

**286. How does the unit define MCP for agent extensibility?**

MCP is a standardized way for agents to retrieve business context, interact with enterprise systems, and maintain consistent reasoning across apps; it also serves as a structured contract for what context an agent can access and how that context should be interpreted. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design extensible agents using MCP in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-extensibility-model-context-protocol-copilot-studio/

**287. What kinds of structured information can MCP expose?**

Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations data entities such as customers, vendors, and products; business process metadata such as workflows, status values, and approval chains; domain models such as financial dimensions and ledger models; and localization rules and taxonomies. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design extensible agents using MCP in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-extensibility-model-context-protocol-copilot-studio/

**288. What governance responsibilities does the unit name for MCP-enabled agents?**

Govern data access by user identity using least privilege, align MCP context boundaries with compliance controls, log agent decisions for auditability, enforce responsible AI behavior in instructions, and establish business and IT ownership through an AI CoE model. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design extensible agents using MCP in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-extensibility-model-context-protocol-copilot-studio/

**289. What can Computer Use do in Copilot Studio?**

It can control the mouse and keyboard, navigate websites and desktop apps, read onscreen text and UI elements, extract text from the screen, follow multi-step UI sequences, and execute tasks across multiple apps. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design agents to automate tasks in apps and websites with Computer Use in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agents-automate-tasks-apps-websites-computer-copilot-studio/

**290. Which scenarios are best suited for Computer Use?**

Scenarios with no API or connector, repetitive UI-driven tasks such as data entry or form submission, tasks that require navigating multiple apps, and situations where human-like reasoning is needed to handle dynamic pages or changing menus. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design agents to automate tasks in apps and websites with Computer Use in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agents-automate-tasks-apps-websites-computer-copilot-studio/

Which apps or sites the agent may access, what data it may interact with, what actions are prohibited, and what time limits or retry limits apply. **292. What four main components shape agent behavior in Copilot Studio?**

Instructions, knowledge, actions and tools, and policies and constraints. [SRC: Design extensibility of AI solutions — Design agent behaviors in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-extensibility-ai-solutions/design-agent-behaviors-copilot-studio-reasoning-voice-mode/

When the solution requires high-precision logic, multi-stage evaluation, recommendations based on historical data, tasks requiring constraints and validation logic, or advanced problem decomposition.
