**314. What are the four benefits of adopting agents into an organization's service structure listed in the Copilot Studio introduction?**

Reducing assisted support inquiries, integrations with other systems, task automation, and generative answers. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/1-introduction/

**315. In Microsoft Copilot Studio, what does an environment represent?**

An environment represents a space to store, manage, and share an organization's business data; every agent, model-driven or canvas app, and Power Automate flow you create is stored in an environment. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Work with environments] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/2-get-started/

**316. Name two organizational patterns for using multiple Copilot Studio environments described in the module.**

Departmental (an environment corresponds to a specific team or department) and locational (a separate environment for different geographic regions); organizations can also separate development, test, and production workloads into different environments. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Work with environments] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/2-get-started/

**317. Can you transfer an existing Copilot Studio agent between the GitHub Copilot harness and the standard harness after it's created?**

No. You choose the harness when you create the agent, and you can't transfer an existing agent between the GitHub Copilot and standard harnesses. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/3-create-bots/

**318. What billing model applies to the GitHub Copilot harness versus the standard harness in Copilot Studio?**

The GitHub Copilot harness bills through Copilot Credits, while the standard harness bills through Copilot Studio licensing and capacity. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/3-create-bots/

**319. What button lets you move an agent you started building in Microsoft 365 Copilot into Copilot Studio for more capabilities?**

The 'Copy to Copilot Studio' button, found in the 'More options (…)' menu when editing the agent, copies the agent to Copilot Studio so you don't need to recreate it. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create and configure declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/declarative-agents/

**320. What are the two ways to create your own declarative agent from scratch in Agent Builder?**

Configure (enter the name, description, and instructions manually) and Describe (use natural language to describe the agent's purpose and let Copilot figure out the rest). [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create and configure declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/declarative-agents/

**321. What are the three ways you can create a Copilot Studio agent according to the module (besides a blank agent)?**

You can describe what your agent needs to do in natural language, install a managed agent, or use one of several prebuilt agent templates — in addition to creating a blank agent. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create and configure agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/create-agents/

**322. What voice modality does a voice-enabled Copilot Studio agent use compared to a chat-based agent?**

A chat-based agent uses text as the default modality, while a voice-enabled agent uses the Speech and DTMF (dual-tone multi-frequency) modality. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create and configure agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/create-agents/

**323. What must you do before you can select the environment used when creating an agent from a blank template in Copilot Studio?**

You enter the agent's name, then expand 'Agent settings (Optional)' to select the Language and Solution and enter the Schema name before selecting Create. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create and configure agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/create-agents/

**324. What are the two types of predefined topics in a standard harness Copilot Studio agent?**

System topics (support essential behaviors like escalation or ending the conversation) and Custom topics (pre-created topics like greeting, goodbye, and start over). [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Work with topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/4-topics/

**325. In classic orchestration, when can actions be invoked according to the orchestration comparison table?**

Actions can only be invoked within a specific topic, whereas in generative orchestration the agent can choose to call tools based on their name and description. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Enhance productivity with generative AI] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/generative-ai/

**326. Name the six types of tools available for agents in Copilot Studio described in the generative AI unit.**

Prompt, Workflow, Computer Use, Connector, REST API, and Model Context Protocol (MCP). [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Enhance productivity with generative AI] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/generative-ai/

**327. What is the activity map in the Copilot Studio Test panel used for?**

The activity map is a visual mapping of the agent's sequence of inputs, decisions, and outputs within a session, shown when 'Show activity map when testing' is turned on for generative AI orchestration testing. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test your agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/5-test-bots/

**328. What testing surfaces does a GitHub Copilot harness agent use, compared to a standard harness agent?**

A GitHub Copilot harness agent uses Preview (interactive testing), Evaluate (test sets), and Monitor (completed tasks and activity); a standard harness agent uses the 'Test your agent' panel with the activity map or topic tracking. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test your agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/5-test-bots/

**329. Who maintains the Copilot Studio Kit, and what is it used for?**

The Power Customer Advisory Team (Power CAT) creates and maintains the Copilot Studio Kit, which equips makers with tools to build, govern, test, and optimize custom agents. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Publish agents and analyze performance] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/6-performance-analysis/

**330. Where do tenant administrators go to review Copilot Studio audit records for compliance purposes?**

Tenant administrators search Microsoft Purview audit records for Copilot Studio activities by logging into the Microsoft Purview portal, selecting Solutions > Explore all, then selecting Audit under Core. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Publish agents and analyze performance] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/6-performance-analysis/

**331. What scenario does the hands-on exercise in the Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio module ask you to build an agent for?**

The exercise has you build a simple agent with generative AI support, then apply what you learned to build an agent to support employees who need help with submitting expense claims, using an agent powered by the standard harness. [SRC: Get started with Microsoft Copilot Studio — Exercise - Create an agent with Microsoft Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/power-virtual-agents-bots/exercise-copilot-studio/

**332. What three main parts does the module say every human conversation has, which agent topics are modeled after?**

Conversation beginning (an initiating event), discussion points (the specific items communicated), and conversation ending (an event that closes the conversation). [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-introduction/

**333. Name one scenario in Copilot Studio where classic orchestration is still required even though generative AI orchestration is preferred.**

Using Copilot Studio for voice agents in Dynamics 365 Contact Center still requires classic orchestration. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Overview of topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-overview/

**334. Under generative AI orchestration, does an agent require custom topics to respond to users?**

No — with generative AI orchestration you can create agents without adding custom topics; the agent uses the knowledge, tools, and workflows added to the agent to respond to user requests instead. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Overview of topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-overview/

**335. What two options are available for creating a new topic in Copilot Studio's Topics tab?**

From blank (create everything yourself, from triggers to conversation flow) or Create from description with Copilot (Copilot generates the topic from a natural-language description you provide). [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Create and configure agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-create/

**336. What does the Code editor feature of the topic designer show, and what is it useful for?**

The Code editor shows the topic in YAML, a markup language that's easy to read and understand; it's used to copy and paste topics from other agents. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Create and configure agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-create/

**337. What does the 'Ask the user before running this tool' topic detail setting control, and what is its default?**

It controls whether the user is prompted to confirm the use of a topic; it's off by default, but should be enabled for sensitive or regulated domains or when making changes on behalf of the user. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Create and configure agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-create/

**338. What are the three base fields every Question node contains?**

Ask a question (the question text), Identify (what the agent should listen for, such as an entity), and Save user response as (how the captured answer is saved as a variable). [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Add conversation nodes to topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-nodes/

**339. What is the difference between the two Skip behavior options on a Question node?**

'Allow question to be skipped' skips the question if its variable already has a value, while 'Ask every time' asks the question even if the variable already has a value. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Add conversation nodes to topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-nodes/

**340. What happens to a quick reply button in the chat history once it has been used?**

The quick reply text is shown in the chat history as if the user typed the message, and the quick reply buttons are removed from the chat history once the agent or user sends another activity. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Add conversation nodes to topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-nodes/

**341. List the seven topic management nodes available in Copilot Studio.**

Go to another topic, Recognize intent, End current topic, End all topics, Transfer conversation, Go to step, and End conversation. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Add conversation nodes to topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-nodes/

**342. When does Copilot Studio automatically add branches to a question node without you manually adding a condition?**

Branches are added automatically whenever you select Multiple Choice options in the Identify field of a question node — each option gets its own branch created for it. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Branch a topic] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-branch/

**343. Can a topic containing errors be saved and deployed to production in Copilot Studio?**

It can be saved, but it can't be deployed to production — errors must be resolved first, while warnings don't block deployment because they don't prevent the agent from functioning. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Manage topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-manage/

**344. What happens when you use 'Make a copy' on a topic in the Topics list page?**

It creates a duplicate of the selected topic with '(Copy)' appended to the name, copying over all topic content including the description, trigger phrases, and the entire conversation. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Manage topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-manage/

**345. What is slot filling in the context of Copilot Studio entities?**

Slot filling is a natural language understanding concept that saves an extracted entity to an object — it matches what a customer inputs and stores it appropriately in a variable, even if a synonym like 'Trekking' was used instead of the defined value 'Hiking.' [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with entities] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/entities/

**346. What is proactive slot filling, and what default Question behavior setting enables it?**

Proactive slot filling lets the agent recognize multiple pieces of information mapped to multiple entities from a single user utterance; it is enabled by the default Question behavior setting 'Allow question to be skipped,' which lets the agent skip a question if the needed value was already provided. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with entities] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/entities/

**347. What is the difference between 'Receive values from other topics' and 'Return values to original topics' for Copilot Studio variables?**

Receive values from other topics lets a redirecting topic pass a value into a variable in the destination topic (skipping re-asking the question); Return values to original topics sends a variable obtained in the redirected topic back to the original topic that redirected to it. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with variables in your Copilot Studio agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/variables/

**348. What setting lets an external source, such as a logged-in website session, initialize a global variable's value before the conversation starts?**

In the Variable properties pane, under Usage, selecting the 'External sources can set value' box lets a global variable be initialized with an external source, such as a customer's name from an already-logged-in website session. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with variables in your Copilot Studio agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/variables/

**349. What variables does the On Error system topic's default message display to the user?**

The default On Error message displays the System.Error.Message, System.Error.Code, and Conversation.Id variables. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with system topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-system/

**350. Why might you disable the Conversation Start system topic, according to the module?**

Turning it off can reduce agent costs, because every agent message — including the welcome message in Conversation Start — consumes Copilot Credits; this is useful when the agent relies only on retrieval-augmented generation and doesn't need extra structured interactions. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with system topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-system/

**351. What variable stores the initial unrecognized text a user entered when the Fallback topic is triggered?**

The UnrecognizedTriggerPhrase variable stores the initial unrecognized text entered by the user. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with system topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-system/

**352. What are the four predefined custom topics in a Copilot Studio agent, and how is Greeting different from Conversation Start?**

The four predefined custom topics are Greeting, Goodbye, Start Over, and Thank you. Greeting responds politely to greeting intents mentioned mid-conversation (like 'Hi'), while Conversation Start automatically fires when the chat window first opens — they are not the same topic. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Work with system topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-system/

**353. What orchestration mode is enabled by default for agents created with the Voice agent template in Copilot Studio?**

Classic orchestration is enabled for agents created with the Voice template. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Topics in a Copilot Studio voice agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-voice/

**354. What does SSML stand for and what does it let you control in a voice-enabled agent's message nodes?**

SSML stands for Speech Synthesis Markup Language, an XML-based markup language that lets you precisely control how text is spoken by a text-to-speech engine, including pitch, rate, volume, pauses, pronunciation, and voice selection. [SRC: Design agent conversations using topics — Topics in a Copilot Studio voice agent] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-topics/topics-voice/

**355. What former name is being replaced by the term 'workflow' in Copilot Studio, per the module's terminology note?**

Microsoft is updating terminology from 'agent flow' to 'workflow'; some current UI elements or older documentation may still show 'agent flow.' [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/introduction/

**356. Do you need a separate Power Automate license to use Copilot Studio workflows as tools, and how is usage billed?**

No separate Power Automate license is needed — billing for Copilot Studio workflows used as tools is based on Copilot Studio usage. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Overview of Copilot Studio workflows as tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/overview-workflow-tools/

**357. What is the 100-second action limit for a Copilot Studio workflow used as a tool, and what can you do if actions need to run longer?**

A workflow must respond to the calling agent within a 100-second action limit; actions that need to run longer can be placed after the Respond to Copilot action to continue running up to the workflow run duration limit of 30 days. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create Copilot Studio workflows as tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/create-workflow-tools/

**358. What must the Asynchronous response toggle be set to for a Copilot Studio workflow tool to respond to the agent in real time?**

The Asynchronous response toggle must be set to Off, found under Networking in the Respond to the agent action settings. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create Copilot Studio workflows as tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/create-workflow-tools/

**359. What are the two ways to create a Copilot Studio workflow described in the module?**

Natural language (describe what you need in everyday language and Copilot Studio interprets your intent and creates the workflow) and Designer (build the workflow by selecting and adding components on a visual canvas). [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Create Copilot Studio workflows as tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/create-workflow-tools/

**360. What icon do you select in a workflow action's input field to insert dynamic content from a previous step's output?**

You select the Insert dynamic content icon, which looks like a lightning bolt; you can also type '/' in the field to open the dynamic content pane. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design Copilot Studio workflow tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/design-workflow-tool-logic/

**361. What connector provides the built-in Condition action used to create branches in a Copilot Studio workflow?**

Conditions are a built-in action from the Control connector, and they create if...then...else branches based on whether a condition is true or false. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design Copilot Studio workflow tools] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/design-workflow-tool-logic/

**362. What are the two 'Fill using' options for how an agent populates a workflow tool's input values?**

Dynamically fill with AI (default, the agent extracts the value from context or asks the user) and Custom value (an explicit fixed value, a variable, or a Power Fx formula). [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot Studio workflows as tools to agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/add-workflow-tools-agents/

**363. What are the four 'After running' completion options for a workflow tool once it finishes?**

Don't respond (default, the agent incorporates the tool output into its own response), Write the response with generative AI, Send specific response, and Send an adaptive card. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot Studio workflows as tools to agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/add-workflow-tools-agents/

**364. List three of the six benefits described for calling Copilot Studio workflows from within a topic rather than relying only on generative orchestration.**

Predictable execution, strong control, reusability, reliability, maintainability, and governance are the six benefits — for example, predictable execution means topics trigger workflows deterministically whereas generative AI may vary. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Add Copilot Studio workflows as tools to topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/add-workflow-tools-topics/

**365. Where can you inspect the inputs and outputs of each step after a Copilot Studio workflow tool has run?**

You can check the workflow run history and select an entry under the start column to inspect the details for each step in the workflow, checking inputs and outputs. [SRC: Add structured automation to agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Test workflow tools in Copilot Studio] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/copilot-studio-structured-automation/test-workflow-tools/

**366. In the module's Contoso HR scenario, what two Copilot Studio capabilities let you go beyond plain text responses?**

Message node formatting (text markup, images, videos, and quick reply buttons) and Adaptive Cards (a visually rich, scannable layout that can also collect structured input in a single interactive form), both without writing code. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/1-introduction

**367. What happens by default when a message node contains more than one image or video card, and how do you switch to seeing all cards at once?**

By default, multiple media cards display in a carousel showing one card at a time with navigation arrows; select a card and switch to List view using the icon in the node's menu bar to display all cards at once. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure message formatting in agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/2-configure-message-formatting

**368. What hosting requirement applies to images and videos added to a message node?**

Images and videos must be hosted at publicly accessible URLs — the agent can't reach files stored on internal servers or behind authentication. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure message formatting in agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/2-configure-message-formatting

**369. What are message variations in a message node, and how does Copilot Studio choose among them?**

Message variations let you define multiple phrasings for a single message node; each time the node runs, Copilot Studio randomly selects one variation to send so repeated interactions feel less mechanical. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Configure message formatting in agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/2-configure-message-formatting

**370. What are the three core areas of the Adaptive Card designer built into Copilot Studio?**

A card preview that shows how the card renders as you build it, an element toolbox where you browse and select card elements, and a properties panel where you configure the selected element. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design informational Adaptive Cards for agent responses] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/3-design-informational-adaptive-cards

**371. What is the recommended approach for making Adaptive Card content reflect runtime values rather than hardcoded text?**

Compute the needed values into topic variables earlier in the topic flow, then reference those variables (via Power Fx) when configuring the card's text-type properties, so Copilot Studio evaluates and substitutes the variable value at render time. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design informational Adaptive Cards for agent responses] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/3-design-informational-adaptive-cards

**372. When should you use Carousel versus List layout for multiple Adaptive Cards in a message node?**

Use Carousel when each card describes a distinct item the user acts on one at a time (cards display side by side with navigation arrows, one visible at a time); use List when the user needs to compare all options at once, since all cards stack vertically. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Design informational Adaptive Cards for agent responses] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/3-design-informational-adaptive-cards

**373. What node type should you use to check whether a user submitted an Ask with Adaptive Card form before continuing, and why?**

Always add a Condition node immediately after an Ask with Adaptive Card node to check whether the required variables contain values, because Copilot Studio doesn't generate any value from an unsubmitted card and downstream nodes expecting those variables would otherwise error. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Collect user input with interactive Adaptive Cards] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/4-collect-input-adaptive-cards

**374. If you leave the default IDs on Adaptive Card input elements, what topic variable names result, and why is this a problem?**

Default IDs like input1, input2, input3, and input4 produce variables such as Topic.input1 and Topic.input2, which are technically correct but hard to work with in subsequent nodes — so descriptive camelCase IDs like leaveType or startDate should be used instead. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Collect user input with interactive Adaptive Cards] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/4-collect-input-adaptive-cards

**375. How can you populate an Input.ChoiceSet's options dynamically instead of hardcoding them?**

Bind a topic variable to the choices property using a Power Fx expression, such as choices: "=Topic.AvailableLeaveTypes", where the variable must be a table with title and value columns. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Collect user input with interactive Adaptive Cards] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/4-collect-input-adaptive-cards

**376. What action type should you use instead of Action.Execute for Adaptive Card buttons on the web channel, and why?**

Use Action.Submit instead of Action.Execute, because the web channel doesn't support Action.Execute. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Apply channel-specific considerations for Adaptive Cards] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/5-adaptive-cards-channel-considerations

**377. Which schema version does the Copilot Studio test pane render Adaptive Cards with, and what limitation does this create?**

The test pane renders cards using the web channel engine, which supports schema version 1.6, so a card using v1.6 features may look correct in the test pane while failing entirely in Teams or Live Chat, which only support v1.5. [SRC: Deliver rich agent responses using Adaptive Cards in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Apply channel-specific considerations for Adaptive Cards] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/deliver-rich-agent-responses-adaptive-cards-copilot-studio/5-adaptive-cards-channel-considerations

**378. What three ways does the module describe for connecting agent topics to external systems in Copilot Studio?**

Adding tools to a topic to perform real-time actions, calling an agent flow to run multi-step automation, and using the HTTP request node to call a REST API directly. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/1-introduction

**379. List the six types of tools Copilot Studio offers for extending a topic, as named in the module.**

Connectors, Agent flows, Prompts, REST APIs (preview), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Computer use (preview). [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Call tools from agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/2-call-tools-topics

**380. How do 'Create search query' and 'Perform custom search' typically work together as topic-level tools?**

Create search query rewrites the user's most recent message into a structured, context-aware query string, and Perform custom search then runs that query against configured knowledge sources and returns the raw, unsummarized results as an output variable for further processing. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Call tools from agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/2-call-tools-topics

**381. What five requirements must an agent flow meet before it can be added to a topic as a callable tool?**

It needs the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger, a 'Respond to the agent' action, the Asynchronous response toggle set to Off, declared input and output parameters, and it must be a solution flow. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Call agent flows from agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/3-call-agent-flows-topics

**382. For a long-running agent flow operation, what pattern lets the topic avoid waiting inline for the entire process to finish?**

Design the flow to start the background operation and immediately return a job ID or tracking reference through Respond to the agent, then run any remaining steps asynchronously afterward (up to Power Automate's flow duration limit of 30 days), while the topic uses a separate polling topic or follow-up message to surface the final outcome. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Call agent flows from agent topics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/3-call-agent-flows-topics

**383. Where should you store API credentials referenced in a Send HTTP Request node's headers, and why?**

Store credentials in environment variables and reference the environment variable in the header value field, because any maker with access to the topic canvas can see hardcoded literal string values, so credentials should never be hardcoded directly in header fields. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Retrieve and send data using the HTTP request node] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/4-configure-http-request-node

**384. What are the three Body options available for the Send HTTP Request node, and when is each used?**

No Content (used with GET requests, no body sent), JSON Content (sends a JSON object, supports static JSON or Power Fx formulas with dynamic topic variables), and Raw content (sends an arbitrary string when the API expects a non-JSON format). [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Retrieve and send data using the HTTP request node] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/4-configure-http-request-node

**385. How do you define the response schema for a Send HTTP Request node so its fields become usable variables?**

Set Response data type to From Sample Data, select Get schema from sample JSON, paste a sample JSON response from the API's documentation, and select Confirm — Copilot Studio then generates a Power Fx variable schema with IntelliSense support. [SRC: Take action from agent conversations using topics and tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio — Retrieve and send data using the HTTP request node] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/take-action-agent-topics-tools-flows-copilot-studio/4-configure-http-request-node

Operational health, performance metrics, quality assurance, usage insights, and risk management. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/1-introduction

Azure Monitor, Microsoft 365 Admin Analytics, and Copilot analytics dashboards (also Power Platform Admin Center). [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Introduction] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/1-introduction

Operational health, performance metrics, quality and output accuracy, usage insights, and risk/compliance/security. Defined roles (ops team, product owners, data engineers, architects), incident response process workflows, standardized metric definitions, log review cadence, change management/version tracking, and documentation of expected agent behaviors. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Recommend process tools for monitoring agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/2-recommend-process-tools-monitoring-agents

**390. What does Azure Monitor provide for AI agent monitoring, per this unit?**

Application and agent telemetry, real-time dashboards, alert rules for anomalies, and integration with Log Analytics Workspaces for KQL-based diagnostics. 2.5 seconds average response time, 17 errors today, and a 'steady' usage trend. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Recommend process tools for monitoring agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/2-recommend-process-tools-monitoring-agents

**392. What five best practices does this unit recommend for monitoring enterprise AI agents?**

Centralize logs, standardize naming conventions, define clear SLAs for agent responsiveness, automate alerting for critical workflows, and integrate monitoring outputs into monthly operational reviews. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Recommend process tools for monitoring agents] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/2-recommend-process-tools-monitoring-agents

**393. What does this unit recommend regarding log review cadence in a monitoring operating model?**

Establish a regular log review cadence — daily, weekly, or monthly — as part of a standardized monitoring operating model. Accuracy and Reasoning, Knowledge Issues, Performance, User Experience, Integration Issues, and Governance and Compliance. Conversation transcripts, agent usage analytics, support tickets, internal surveys, in-app rating prompts, and observability dashboards. Identify training or knowledge updates needed, recommend guardrail adjustments or action limits, and build an Agent Improvement Plan. **397. In the Agent Health Summary table for this unit, what were the Finance Assistant's success rate and average response time?**

96% success rate with a 2.1 second average response time and 8 issues logged. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Analyze backlog and user feedback for AI agent usage] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/3-analyze-backlog-user-feedback-ai-agent-usage

**398. What is the first stage of the 'Feedback-to-Improvement' pipeline described in this unit?**

Operational Health, Quality of Reasoning, Knowledge Coverage, User Experience, and Governance & Compliance Signals. Knowledge Tuning, Behavioral Tuning, Performance Tuning, and Governance-Aligned Tuning. Correct the API or connector settings. No unauthorized actions — the agent must never perform disallowed operations. **403. What three metrics make up the 'User-Centered Metrics' category for monitoring AI agents?**

Satisfaction Indicators, Abandonment Rate, and Task Completion Rate. [SRC: Monitor, analyze, and tune AI agents — Monitor AI agent performance metrics] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/analyze-monitor-tune-ai-powered-business-solutions/5-monitor-agent-performance-metrics

**404. What three signs indicate 'Model Drift' in a deployed AI agent?**

Shifts in response patterns, declining accuracy in recurring tasks, and increased hallucination or off-topic responses. **500. What is a patch solution used for in Power Platform ALM?**

**501. Across which boundaries can Power Platform solutions be deployed?**

**502. What is the Microsoft Power Platform CLI and what does it provide?**

[SRC: From Introduction to solutions for Microsoft Power Platform Module Assessment] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-solutions/check/

**503. What does the 'solution unpack' command do?**

The 'solution unpack' command reversibly decomposes a solution .zip file into a logical folder structure, making it human-readable and suitable for version control integration with Git and other tools. This enables collaborative ALM practices and source control management. [SRC: From Introduction to solutions for Microsoft Power Platform Module Assessment] | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-solutions/check/
